text.en: The Marathas are people of the Deccan plateau, identified with the Marathi language. In the 17th century a young leader named Shivaji began to build a new kind of kingdom.

The Marathas are people from the Deccan, especially present-day Maharashtra, identified by the Marathi language with a rich literature since the 12th century.
In the 13th century the Yadavas ruled from Devagiri, and later the Khalji Sultanate of Delhi defeated them.
Bhakti saints such as Dnyaneshwar, Tukaram and Ramdas spread messages of devotion and equality in the Marathi language.
Shivaji Bhonsle was born around 1630 and learned values and administration from his mother Jijabai and his teachers.
He captured forts, built a strong navy and used guerrilla warfare, with quick surprise attacks in hilly land.
In 1674 he was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad, and he set up a council of ministers called the Ashta Pradhan.
His administration protected farmers, paid officials in cash, and respected all religions.
After Shivaji (died 1680) and Aurangzeb's wars in the Deccan, Maratha power passed to the Peshwas, ministers who became rulers.
In the 18th century the Marathas spread across large parts of India but were defeated at the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.
The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in 1818 with the British defeating the Marathas.

prompt.en: What helped Shivaji build a kingdom?

requiredIdeas.en: Support of people and saints' ideas.

points.en: The Marathas of the Deccan rose under Shivaji.
Shivaji was crowned in 1674 and built forts, a navy and an administration.
The Peshwas expanded Maratha power until 1818.
